title: Tenant-isolated admission control and lightweight snapshotting for console ingest
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: High-cardinality console metrics ingestion is vulnerable to noisy tenants and bursty routes that cause tail latency and cascading retries. Existing global admission policies either over-throttle light-weight tenants or allow noisy tenants to monopolize local memory and CPU, causing downstream backpressure.

Goal: Implement a tenant-aware admission controller in the ingest gateway and a lightweight snapshotting commit flow in the per-shard stream processor so we can: (1) isolate noisy tenants at the gateway level with tenant-level token buckets and dynamic cost weights, (2) provide fast local snapshot isolation for stateful enrichments and windowed aggregations to enable quick failover and replay, and (3) allow safe burst spills to object storage without violating per-tenant SLOs.

Scope: Gateway admission control, per-shard in-memory quotas, snapshot format and commit cadence, spill-to-object-storage policy, monitoring and SLO dashboards, gradual rollout plan with canary per-tenant. Excludes long-term archival retention and cross-region replication (handled by separate project).

Design summary:
- Admission controller at edge: per-tenant token bucket + dynamic cost-weight calculated from recent per-tenant token consumption and per-route cost profile (compute vs storage heavy). Controller exposes a low-overhead gRPC hook for route metadata augmentation.
- Local quota enforcement: each shard maintains a resident per-tenant soft quota; when exceeded, requests are either delayed (priority queue), downgraded (sampled), or spilled. Policy is configurable per-customer tier.
- Lightweight snapshotting: introduce incremental in-shard checkpoints representing application-level offsets and a delta log. Checkpoints are small JSON+binary blobs stored in durable object store with metadata pointing to last stable offset; recovery only needs last checkpoint + deltas. Snapshots are atomic at raft-shard boundary to avoid cross-shard consistency complexity.
- Spill policy: prioritize tenant-preserving semantics: spill only the lowest-priority tenant partitions first and keep high-priority tenant windows in memory. Spilled data is kept for replay windows (48h) and can be re-ingested using the delta log.

Trade-offs considered:
- Stronger cross-shard snapshotting (global consistent snapshot) was rejected for complexity and latency cost.
- Per-tenant exact accounting adds CPU overhead; we rely on approximate counters and exponentially-weighted moving averages to reduce cost.
- Snapshot frequency tuned to balance recovery latency vs durable write cost; starting default is 5 minutes for shards with >1M events/min, 15 minutes otherwise.

Rollout plan: 1) feature-flagged in staging with synthetic noisy tenants, 2) canary 2 selected low-impact customers for 48h, 3) enable for all trial accounts, 4) open rollout to paid tiers with opt-in, 5) enable default for new tenants after two weeks of monitoring and tuning.

Metrics to monitor: per-tenant 99th latency at gateway, per-shard memory pressure, rate of spills (per-tenant), replays/sec, snapshot write latency, consumer lag after failover.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces per-tenant token buckets with configurable rate/cost weights and reduces noisy-tenant 99p gateway latency by >30% in synthetic tests
When shard memory pressure crosses threshold, lower-priority tenant partitions are spilled with <5s added latency for high-priority tenants
Recovery from last checkpoint + deltas restores in-shard state within target RTO of 90s for shards with steady 500k events/min
End-to-end tests for replay and snapshotting exist and are part of CI with synthetic noisy streams
Monitoring dashboards for spill rate, per-tenant latency, and snapshot health are available in console-2025.04 release
tasks: implement gateway admission controller gRPC hook and token-bucket logic
add per-shard tenant quota tracking and priority queue
implement incremental snapshot writer and retention lifecycle
e2e tests: failover restore + tenant replay
run staging load tests with synthetic noisy tenants
dashboard panels and alerts for spill-rate and snapshot-failures
comments: 2025-02-25 | Ava Martinez: Ticket created after triage — aligning with Console Ingest v2 roadmap. Initial design doc linked.
2025-02-27 | Rohit Patel: Prototype of gateway hook implemented. Early tests show ~28% reduction in 99p latency for a single noisy tenant when applying cost-weight=2. Added sample config to PR.
2025-03-01 | Mei Chen (SRE): Reviewed snapshot format — requested adding explicit schema version and faster header checks to avoid cold-path JSON parsing on hot writes.
2025-03-02 | Rohit Patel: Addressed Mei's comments; snapshot header now binary-encoded with version and CRC32. Updated design doc and PRs. Performance microbenchmarks added to PR notes.

2025-03-03 | Product (Liam O'Connor): Please include migration plan for legacy processors. Recommend a delegation mode where legacy processors forward tenant IDs to the new gateway for policy enforcement while snapshots are phased in. Added as task.
last_decision: Use per-shard lightweight snapshots + delta logs (not global consistent snapshot). Prioritize tenant-preserving spills and use EWMA counters for accounting to limit CPU overhead.
notes: This ticket is sensitive to observable accuracy and SLOs — any change must be accompanied by canary dashboards. If spills exceed expected thresholds in canary, rollback immediately and open incident review.
